who: Shunryu Suzuki · Zen Mind, Beginner's Mind, 1970
quote: Those who can sit perfectly physically usually take more time to obtain the true way of Zen... But those who find great difficulties in practicing Zen will find more meaning in it.
meaning: When it is hard, you find more meaning in every step.

who: Doctrine of the Mean, ch. 20 · tr. Ku Hung-ming, 1906
quote: Some exercise these moral qualities naturally and easily; ... some with effort and difficulty. But when the achievement is made it comes to one and the same thing.
meaning: Some find it easy. Some find it hard. In the end, both arrive at the same place.

who: Mencius · Mengzi VII.A.18, tr. James Legge
quote: Men who are possessed of intelligent virtue and prudence in affairs will generally be found to have been in sickness and troubles.
meaning: Wise and careful people usually learned it in hard times.
Iron becomes steel only after a long time in the fire.

quote: No one knows how difficult anything is until he has tried to do it.
meaning: You only know how hard something is when you try it yourself.

who: Japanese proverb · tr. W. G. Aston, 1872
quote: By pinching yourself understand the pain of others.
meaning: Feel the hard part in your own body, and you will understand how hard it is for others.

who: Krishna · Bhagavad Gita 18.37, tr. K. T. Telang, 1882
quote: That happiness is called good, in which one is pleased after repetition... which is like poison first and comparable to nectar in the long run...
meaning: Good things taste bitter at first and sweet at the end. Practice is like that.

who: The Buddha · Dhammapada 80, tr. F. Max Müller, 1881
quote: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.
meaning: Water, arrows and wood are shaped by skilled hands. Wise people shape themselves, bit by bit.

who: Book of Rites (Liji), Record on Education · tr. James Legge, 1885
quote: ...when he learns, one knows his own deficiencies; when he teaches, he knows the difficulties of learning. ... Hence it is said, 'Teaching and learning help each other.'
meaning: Learning shows you what you lack. Teaching shows you how hard learning is.

who: Zeno on his student Cleanthes · Diogenes Laertius 7.37, tr. R. D. Hicks, 1925
quote: ...him Zeno used to compare to hard waxen tablets which are difficult to write upon, but retain the characters written upon them.
meaning: Some learn slowly, like hard wax that is tough to write on. But what they learn stays. Cleanthes later led Zeno's school.
